# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP DRAWING GAMES
*The primary objective is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell the loop uses
- **Masyu** — Loop must satisfy black circle (turn + straight) and white circle (straight + turn neighbor) constraints

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop with Regional Rules
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop traverses cells; bold-line regions require uniformly straight or uniformly turning behavior at white circles
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop traverses rooms once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms

#### 1.3 Loop with Movement/Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction constrained by wind arrows in black cells; loop cannot move against wind

#### 1.4 Loop with Gate/Sequence Constraints
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all gates exactly once in a specified order

#### 1.5 Loop with Geometric Point Constraints
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through all black circles with the circle as the exact midpoint of a straight segment

#### 1.6 Loop with Avoidance and Counting Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered arrow cells; arrow numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction

---

### 2. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*The primary objective is to draw paths or connections between elements without forming a closed loop*

#### 2.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count must match island number; all islands connected

#### 2.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching numbered pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill the grid

---

### 3. CELL SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*The primary objective is to determine which cells to colour black (or shade)*

#### 3.1 Shading with Connectivity and Adjacency Rules
- **Nurikabe** — Numbered white islands separated by a connected black "wall"; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Rooms contain specified counts of black cells; no two adjacent black cells; white cells connected and cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; no two adjacent black cells; white cells connected
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total visible white cells (horizontally + vertically); black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected
- **Usowan** — Shade cells under adjacency rules; each bold-line rectangle contains exactly one "wrong" number clue

#### 3.2 Shading with Rectangular/Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must not be rectangles/squares; numbers indicate region size
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangular half-cell shading so remaining white areas form only rectangles/squares; numbered cells indicate adjacent triangle count

#### 3.3 Shading with Tetromino Rules
- **LITS** — Shade exactly four connected cells (tetromino) per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; all shaded cells connected; no 2×2 shading
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of adjacent black cells) so each bold-line region contains exactly two black cells

#### 3.4 Shading with Sum/Count Constraints from Circles
- **Kurotto** — Circles indicate the total count of connected black cells extending from them; cells with circles stay white

#### 3.5 Shading as Maze Construction
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create a maze from S to G; all circle cells on shortest path; no triangle cells on shortest path; no 2×2 uniformly shaded/unshaded blocks

#### 3.6 Shading with Gravity/Drop Constraints
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per count clues; when all shaded cells "drop" downward they must fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

#### 3.7 Shading by Tile Rules
- **Tilepaint** — Whole bold-line tiles are entirely shaded or unshaded; diagonal-number clues indicate shaded cell counts in a row/column segment; solution depicts an object

---

### 4. REGION / AREA DIVISION GAMES
*The primary objective is to partition the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

#### 4.1 Division into Uniform-Number Blocks
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbers; connected same-number groups must contain exactly that many cells; same-sized groups cannot touch
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

#### 4.2 Division into Fixed-Size Blocks
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell

#### 4.3 Division into L-Shaped Blocks
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped (one-cell-wide) blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows mark an end pointing toward the bend; circled numbers indicate block size

#### 4.4 Division into Symmetric Paired Regions
- **Double Choco** — Divide grid into blocks each containing one white sub-region and one gray sub-region of identical shape (rotation/reflection allowed); numbers indicate sub-region cell count

#### 4.5 Division with Block-Chain Constraints
- **Chained Block** — Shade blocks of consecutive cells; numbered/? cells identify block size; all blocks must form chains (corner-touching); no two blocks of the same size/shape in one chain

#### 4.6 Division with Twin-Block Rules
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two equal-sized shaded blocks that do not touch each other; all shaded cells connected across regions; no 2×2 fully shaded

---

### 5. NUMBER / SYMBOL PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary objective is to place numbers or symbols into cells satisfying given constraints*

#### 5.1 Latin-Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in every row, column, and 3×3 box without repetition

#### 5.2 Room-Based Sequential Numbering
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1…n (n = room size); duplicate values in a row/column must be separated by at least that many cells
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1…n; arrow black cells indicate which neighbor holds the room's maximum value; no identical numbers in adjacent rooms

#### 5.3 Directional Symbol Fill
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; bold-line territory numbers indicate excess of one symbol; — cannot span more than two rows vertically; | cannot span more than two columns horizontally

#### 5.4 Cross-Word Style Number Fill
- **Nansuke** — Fill white cells with digits forming numbers from a provided list; numbers run horizontally or vertically; each cell holds one digit

#### 5.5 Snake Placement
- **Hebi** — Place numbered snakes (1=head … 5=tail) in white cells; snakes cannot share sides; line-of-sight rules prevent one snake from "seeing" another in its forward direction; black-cell clues give nearest snake-part value in arrow direction

---

### 6. OBJECT / PIECE PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary objective is to place discrete objects or pieces into the grid*

#### 6.1 Light Bulb Placement
- **Akari** — Place bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell illuminated; no bulb illuminates another bulb

#### 6.2 Evolving Block Placement (Polyomino Growth)
- **Evolomino** — Draw squares in white cells forming blocks; each block contains one arrow; each successive block along an arrow's path adds one cell to the previous block's shape without rotation/flip

#### 6.3 Pencil/Line Piece Placement
- **Pencils** — Identify straight pencil pieces ending at a tip; draw a non-crossing, non-branching line from each tip through as many cells as the pencil's number indicates

---

### 7. MOVEMENT / MIGRATION GAMES
*The primary objective is to move existing elements to satisfy destination constraints*

#### 7.1 Circle Migration to Countries
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally/vertically so each bold-line country contains exactly one circle; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross

#### 7.2 Circle Migration to Gray Areas
- **Yosenabe** — Move all circles straight into gray areas; arrow tips land in gray cells; numbered gray areas must receive circles whose values sum to the area's number; paths cannot cross

---

### 8. HYBRID / COMPOUND GAMES
*Games combining two or more substantially different mechanics*

#### 8.1 Shading + Loop
- **Yajilin** *(also listed under Loop)* — Determine black cell placement AND draw a loop through remaining non-clue cells

#### 8.2 Shading + Promontory (Connectivity + Shape)
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells so circled cells are "promontories" (exactly one white neighbor); numbered circles indicate straight-line white run length; white cells connected; no 2×2 uniform blocks

#### 8.3 Number Fill + Directional Clues (Visibility)
- **Kurodoko** *(also listed under Shading)* — Combines number-visibility counting with black-cell placement

---

## Cross-Cutting Constraint Dimensions

| Dimension | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Connectivity required (white/unshaded)** | Nurikabe, Hitori, Kurodoko, Heyawake, Nurimisaki |
| **No 2×2 uniform blocks** | Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki |
| **Adjacency prohibition (black cells)** | Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Yajilin, Usowan |
| **Single closed loop** | Slitherlink, Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Mid-loop, Yajilin |
| **Bold-line regions as primary structure** | Heyawake, Ripple Effect, Makaro, LITS, Double Choco, Five Cells, Nuritwin, Norinori, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Juosan |
| **Arrow / directional clues** | Yajilin, Hebi, Makaro, Sashigane, Yosenabe, Evolomino |
| **Path non-crossing constraint** | Numberlink, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Hashiwokakero |
